intro: On the slope above the Meander gorge stands the Sanctuary of Apollo Lairbenos, a sanctuary in Denizli province from the 2nd century BC. Its temple has left us something rare: hundreds of confession inscriptions, the frankest record of popular religion in the Roman countryside.
history: This temple, on the slope above the Meander gorge, grew up where a local Anatolian god came to be identified with Apollo. Hundreds of inscriptions from here record, plainly and by name, the offences of people whom the god had punished with illness or misfortune. These are the so-called confession inscriptions.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the temple foundations, the confession inscriptions, the temenos wall and the rock-cut steps.
facts: Did you know? The confession inscriptions let the ordinary people of the Roman countryside tell us their beliefs in their own words. The offences recorded most often are theft, false oaths and breaches of temple rules. Hundreds of these inscriptions come from here, each plainly recording the offences of someone the god had punished.
outro: This brings our tour of the Sanctuary of Apollo Lairbenos to an end. Please leave the stones untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water. The voices on these stones confessed long ago; listen to them kindly. Enjoy your visit.
